output.summary: Deciduous tree native to China, the Japanese persimmon has broad, stiff leaves and sweet, slightly tangy fruit. Astringent varieties are edible only when soft-ripe, while non-astringent varieties such as ‘Fuyu’ can be eaten firm.
output.edibilityNote: The fruit is eaten ripe or dried; astringent varieties require soft ripening, while non-astringent varieties may be eaten firm.
